'''John William Daly''' (June 8, 1933 – March 5, 2008<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/><ref name=NAS/>) was an award-winning American natural products chemist, pharmacologist, and biochemist, and a leading authority on [[amphibian]] [[alkaloid]]s and other areas of [[natural product]]s chemistry. He conducted essentially all of his seminal research as a staff member at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in [[Bethesda, Maryland]], over a period of fifty years. His awards include the [[Ernest Guenther Award|Ernest Guenther Award for Achievements in the Chemistry of Natural Products]] from the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2002, the Norman R. Farnsworth Research Achievement Award of the [[American Society of Pharmacognosy]] in 1997, [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Meritorious Award]] in 1998, and election to the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]], also in 1997.<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/><ref name=Garraffo2008/>

==Early life and education==
{{expand section | with = further usual detail regarding family and early education | small = no|date=February 2026}} 

Daly earned [[bachelor of science]] and [[master of arts]] degrees from Oregon State College (now [[Oregon State University]]), in [[biochemistry]] (1954) and [[organic chemistry]] (1955), respectively.<ref name=Garraffo2008/><ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> He then went on to do his doctoral work at [[Stanford University]], receiving his [[Ph.D.]], also in organic chemistry, in 1958.<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/><ref name=Garraffo2008/>

==Research career==
Daly performed research for nearly 50 years at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in [[Bethesda, Maryland]]. Primary foci of his research included the discovery, structure elucidation, synthesis, and pharmacology of [[alkaloid]]s and other biologically active natural products. He was the world's leading authority in amphibian alkaloids and an expert in many areas of natural products.<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/><ref name=Garraffo2008/>{{verification needed|date=February 2026}}

Daly was a prolific writer, producing around 700 papers, including books and chapters.<ref name=Garraffo2008>{{cite journal |last1=Garraffo |first1=H. Martin |title=John William Daly, 1933–2008 |journal=[[Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology]] |date=2008 |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=439–440 |doi=10.1007/s10571-008-9280-3|pmid=18404366 |s2cid=39229486 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1232796 |pmc=11505825 }}</ref><ref name=JacobsonKirk2009>{{cite journal |last1=Jacobson |first1=Kenneth A. |last2=Kirk |first2=Kenneth L. |title=John W. Daly - An Appreciation |journal=[[Heterocycles_(journal)]] |date=2009 |volume=79 |issue=1 |pages=61–71 |doi=10.3987/COM-08-S(D)Memoire-1|pmid=26160996 |pmc=4493916 }}</ref>{{verification needed|date=February 2026}} He was also a member of the Editorial Board of the scientific journal [[Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology]], since its inception in 1980.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Saavedra |first=Juan M. |date=June 2009 |title=In Memoriam: John William Daly (1933-2008) |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11505801/ |journal=Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=441–442 |doi=10.1007/s10571-008-9334-6 |issn=1573-6830 |pmc=11505801 |pmid=19109768}}</ref> 

==Awards and recognition==
Daly's receiving the [[Ernest Guenther Award|Ernest Guenther Award for Achievements in the Chemistry of Natural Products]] from the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2002 was among the last of a long series of recognitions for the scientist before his death, and it bracketed his receipt of the Hillebrand Award of that Society's Washington, D.C. Section in 1978.<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> Other ways in which he was recignized included the [[Scheele Award|Karl Wilhelm Scheele Award]] of the [https://www.lakemedelsakademin.se/en/home/about-us/ Swedish Academy of Pharmaceutical Sciences] in 1999,<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> the [[Norman R. Farnsworth Research Achievement Award]] of the [[American Society of Pharmacognosy]] in 1997,<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/><ref>{{cite web |author = ASP Staff | date = 2026 | orig-date= 1997 | title=Norman R Farnsworth Research Achievement Award Recipients... John W Daly | work = [[Pharmacognosy]].us | url = https://www.pharmacognosy.us/grants-and-awards/grants-and-awards-archive/research-achievement-award/norman-r-farnsworth-research-achievement-award-recipients/ | access-date = February 14, 2026 | location = Northbrook, IL | publisher = The American Society of Pharmacognosy (ASP)}}</ref> and his recognition by his employer, the [[United States Government]], with the 1998 [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Meritorious Award]].<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> He became a Scientist Emeritus at the NIH in 2003.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Garraffo |first=H. Martin |date=2008-04-11 |title=John William Daly, 1933–2008 |url=https://europepmc.org/api/getPdf?pmcid=PMC11505825 |journal=Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology}}</ref>

Daly was elected to the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1997, his stated sections being, first, "[[physiology]] and [[pharmacology]]", and second, "[[chemistry]]".<ref name=NAS>{{cite web | author = NAS Staff | date= March 5, 2008 | title=John W. Daly | work = [[National Academy of Sciences|U.S. NAS]] (NASOnline.org) | format = member database entry | url = https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/john-w-daly-e1qtdk/ | access-date = February 14, 2026 | location = Washington, D.C. | publisher = [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS)}}</ref><ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> This coincided with his election as a Corresponding Member of the [[Argentina|Argentine]] <!--Wikilink markup not functioning per guideline: {{ill|Academia Nacional de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|es}}-->[https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academia_Nacional_de_Ciencias_Exactas,_Físicas_y_Naturales Academia Nacional de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales] in that same year,<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/> and it followed his election as a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1991.<ref name=JacobsonKirk2009/>

== Personal life ==
Daly died on March 5, 2008 due to [[pancreatic cancer]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NIH VideoCast - Tribute to John William Daly: A Life Dedicated to Chemistry in Nature |url=https://videocast.nih.gov/watch/9c27d28c-d5db-11f0-9cf9-12c45c580ad9 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=NIH VideoCast |language=en}}</ref>
